record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For MAX-CUT, where the input is an n-vertex graph G = (V, E) and the task is to find a subset X of V that maximizes the number of edges between X and V - X, construct an exact algorithm running in O*(1.99^n) time and using only polynomial space, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Construct an O*(1.99n) time and polynomial space algorithm for MAX-CUT.

artifact.self_contained_problem: The MAX-CUT problem is defined as follows: given an undirected graph G = (V, E) on n = |V| vertices, find a subset X ⊆ V that maximizes the cardinality of the cut |{ {u,v} ∈ E : u ∈ X, v ∈ V \ X }|, i.e., the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in X. Using the O*(·) notation, which suppresses factors polynomial in n, design an exact (deterministic or randomized) algorithm that solves MAX-CUT on arbitrary n-vertex graphs in time O*(1.99^n) while using only space polynomial in n, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search indicates that the existence of a polynomial-space exact algorithm for MAX-CUT running faster than O*(2^n) on arbitrary graphs is still an open problem. Improvements are known for restricted classes (sparse, bounded-degree, split graphs) and faster exponential-space algorithms (e.g., Williams' O*(2^{ωn/3}) approach) exist, but a polynomial-space O*(1.99^n) algorithm for general MAX-CUT has not been reported.

status_evidence.title: Maximum cut - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Whether a polynomial space algorithm for MaxCut exists that runs faster than O*(2^n) is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a sub-2^n polynomial-space algorithm for MAX-CUT on general graphs is open.

status_evidence.title: Exact Algorithms for MaxCut on Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: O*(1.42^n) time algorithm for the Maximum Cut problem on split graphs using polynomial space.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-space exponential-time improvements are known only for restricted graph classes, not general MAX-CUT.
